## Context
The box fixture in tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py constructs env = dict(os.environ) and returns that mapping inside the fixture value. When a test fails, pytest renders the fixture argument and can print ambient credential values into local or CI logs. This was directly observed during a deliberate defect-seeded RED run; no credential value is recorded on this ticket. The performance ticket must not absorb an unrelated security fix.

## Plan
- Reproduce with a synthetic sentinel secret in the ambient environment and a deliberate assertion failure.
- Change the fixture boundary to pass only required environment variables or use a representation-safe wrapper while preserving the real bash subprocess environment needed by the tests.
- Audit sibling subprocess fixtures for the same dict(os.environ)-inside-rendered-fixture shape.
- Prove the synthetic sentinel never appears in pytest failure output while the autodeploy suite remains behaviorally green.

## Scope and alternative rationale
The construct sweep separates two runtime carriers rather than deferring equivalent leaks. This parent and child dumbstruck-wonderful-xiphosuran own the eight decorated fixtures whose returned values pytest renders as function arguments; explicit allowlists are correct there because minimal-parent runs prove their consumers need only declared harness values. The remaining broad mappings are test-local or helper values exposed only when subprocess startup itself raises. Some intentionally forward the invoking pytest environment or environment-only live-service credentials, so applying the fixture allowlist would break their contract. Follow-up antiutopic-toadyish-goldfinch owns all 103 of those sites as one atomic shared representation-safe mapping migration, with a repository guard and exact child-value preservation test. A repo-wide allowlist was rejected because it would drop required values; independent per-file wrappers were rejected because they would duplicate the same diagnostic boundary without enforcement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] A deterministic regression test fails before the fix because a synthetic ambient secret appears in captured pytest failure rendering.

- [x] The synthetic secret is absent from failure output after the fix.
- [x] Required PATH and autodeploy environment behavior remains covered through the real bash subprocess.
- [x] Sibling occurrences are inventoried and either fixed or linked as follow-ups.
- [x] [operator-attested] Repository gates and Gerrit votes pass before closure.
